review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib.mjs:62 The SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers are installed before the readiness loop. On an early-exit or timeout path, `cleanup()` removes them. However, in `startPreview` the `stop` function checks only `exited`, which is set on the child's 'exit' event. If `process.kill(-child.pid)` fails (e.g. the group is gone), it falls back to `child.kill`. This is fine, but `process.exit(130)` in `onSignal` runs while verify's `finally` (browser.close) never executes, which leaks the Chromium process on Ctrl-C.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib.mjs:81 The readiness probe `fetch(`${base}/`)` has no timeout. If the port is bound but the server accepts and never responds, the fetch hangs forever and the 100-iteration loop never reaches its 'did not become ready' error. verify/inspect hang indefinitely and leak the preview process.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs:105 `await page.goto(...)` and `page.waitForSelector` happen inside the try, but a missing or unregistered slug is not detected. The preview serves index.html for any path, so the app falls back to Landing and `waitForSelector(root)` times out with a raw Playwright timeout error (printed as a stack under phase=unexpected). The user gets no hint that the slug is unregistered.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/scaffold.mjs:196 `safeTitle` strips only some characters and is then interpolated into a single-quoted TS string in the registry (`title: '${safeTitle}'`) and into JSX attribute `title=\"{{title}}\"` in Talk.tsx and into a CSS comment (`/* ... \"{{title}}\" ... */`). A title containing `*/` (not stripped) ends the CSS comment early and breaks styles.css. The transition check at verify.mjs:44-50 compares the raw attribute string to String(i) and does not convert it to a number, so an absent attribute (null) never matches and the check times out with a render error naming the step. (3) A non-zero exit is guaranteed: lines 118-123 print `FAIL phase=render step=N` and set exitCode = 1. The focused test at verify.test.ts:71-75 breaks next() so the step index never advances, then asserts a non-zero exit and /FAIL phase=render step=2: .*transition did not advance/. Judge B&#39;s objection is that step 1&#39;s data-step-index is never checked. That does not decide the requirement. Step 1 involves no transition, so nothing is counted as progress there, and no Number(null) === 0 comparison exists. If the index hook were missing, the first real transition (to step 2) would compare null with &#39;1&#39; and fail. So the failure modes the guidance names are both prevented. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[{"id":"skill-empty-directory-scaffold","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The auditor&#39;s facts are accurate. scaffold() copies filesFor(&#39;index&#39;), which includes everything under src/presentations/. The registry registers getting-started, and that presentation&#39;s styles.css sets colors, system-ui fonts, borders and backgrounds. But this does not defeat the pass on this criterion. The scenario this criterion tests asks for a full scaffold of build setup, scene kit and presentation index, with the required dependencies installed, before the presentation is created. Its review guidance lists exactly what to check: the template holds all three anchors and the dependency set; SKILL.md directs a full scaffold and an install; a test materializes the template in a fresh location and builds it; the scene-kit snapshot matches the canonical kit; and Chromium is installed or checked for. Style neutrality is not on that list. The contract scores it under its own criterion, skill-scaffold-style-neutral, whose guidance is to inspect the template&#39;s dependencies and styles. The styling the auditor cites also sits in a file owned by the presentation, which the fixture allows for presentation styling. The scene kit and src/index.css stay free of visual defaults. So even if this clause counted against skill-scaffold-style-neutral, it would not make this criterion&#39;s scenario unmet. A fact the requirement does not depend on cannot turn this pass into a fail.","evidence":["The criterion&#39;s scenario is: WHEN the skill runs in an empty or unscaffolded directory THEN it performs a full scaffold (build setup, scene kit, presentation index) and installs dependencies. Its…","Style neutrality has its own criterion, skill-scaffold-style-neutral, whose guidance is to inspect the bootstrap&#39;s dependencies and styles.","templates/bootstrap/src/presentations/getting-started/styles.css is owned by the presentation; its header comment reads &#39;Owned by this presentation, not the kit: restyle freely.&#39;","The bootstrap kit&#39;s Box.tsx describes itself as &#39;Carries identity and style hooks, no styling&#39;. tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts asserts that src/index.css contains no font-family, hex…","SKILL.md says a fresh scaffold adds a getting-started starter that the user may keep or delete."],"citations":["skills/presentation/scripts/scaffold.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentations/getting-started/styles.css","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentations/getting-started/Talk.tsx","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentations/index.ts","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","skills/presentation/SKILL.md","tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-tests-isolate-resources","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The material does show that the arrow test calls startPreview() and launchBrowser() before its try/finally, so a Chromium launch failure would skip the test&#39;s preview.stop(). But this criterion&#39;s guidance says &#39;a missing browser installation is not scored here&#39;, and that is exactly the case where launchBrowser throws. The guidance names only two fail cases: a shared hardcoded port, and killing only the npx wrapper. The rules forbid failing on a scenario the guidance doesn&#39;t name. On every path the test actually produces, it stops the real Vite process (spawned directly through process.execPath and killed by process group) and closes the browser in finally. Ports are dynamic. So the pass verdict stands.","evidence":["bootstrap.test.ts arrow test: `const preview = await startPreview(); const browser = await launchBrowser(); try { ... } finally { await browser.close(); preview.stop() }`.","lib.mjs launchBrowser throws CheckError(&#39;browser&#39;, &#39;could not launch Chromium ...&#39;) only when the Chromium launch fails, which is the missing-browser case the guidance excludes (&#39;…","lib.mjs startPreview spawns `process.execPath vite.js preview` detached and stops it with process.kill(-child.pid, &#39;SIGTERM&#39;). This kills the real server, not an npm/npx wrapper.","lib.mjs freePort uses server.listen(0, HOST), so preview ports are allocated dynamically.","verify.test.ts checks with pgrep that no vite.js process remains after each fault run, including the browser launch failure run."],"citations":["tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib.mjs","tests/integration/verify.test.ts"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
